title: tooling(pm): the fleet relay may start release.yml with refresh_version_pr true alone, so a seat refreshes the Version PR through the relay
body:
Fixes #23193
Clause-②: no

## What this changes

`WORKFLOW_DISPATCH_ALLOWLIST` in `scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs` is now the key set of a new table, `WORKFLOW_DISPATCH_INPUTS`: every allowlisted workflow carries its ONE closed inputs object beside its name. `release.yml` joins with exactly `{ refresh_version_pr: true }`. `shard-timings-refresh.yml` stays `null`: it declares no inputs, so an action naming it carries no `inputs` key.

The ruling this executes is #23177 ruling **B** (comment 6139629628, the maintainer's 「同意」), item 5, verbatim:

> **Operational, on the release path:** after each fix merges to `main`, the acting seat dispatches `Release` with `refresh_version_pr` through the relay at once rather than waiting for the 6-hourly refresh.

The seat's stroke is one actions file:

```json
[{ "op": "workflow_dispatch", "workflow": "release.yml", "ref": "main", "inputs": { "refresh_version_pr": true } }]
```

## The card's "What done looks like", line by line

- **`release.yml` joins the allowlist with exactly one input, `refresh_version_pr: true`.** The `workflow_dispatch` row gains one optional key, `inputs`, a new field kind (a JSON object of input name to boolean). It also gains a row property, `closedInputs`, that the validator judges against the file's entry: exactly that object, every key and every value.
- **`force` is refused, and so are `refresh_version_pr: false`, an absent input and any other input.** `closedInputsErrors` in `validate.mjs` refuses each one by name, and reports every reason in one pass. The string `"true"` is refused once, as the field kind: the payload has one spelling. The executor re-judges the stroke and exits 2 before its sender gate, so a refused stroke sends zero requests of any kind. The seat's CLI refuses the same strokes before anything is sent (exit 2).
- **The relay can start only the bookkeeping lane.** This is measured against `release.yml`'s own guards, not recalled. The validator self-test reads the file's `workflow_dispatch` inputs (`force` and `refresh_version_pr`, both boolean, both defaulting to false). It then evaluates every job's `if:` for the relay's dispatch, in `needs` order and with three-valued logic, so a guard it cannot decide reads as "may run" and never as "skipped". The result: `version-pr` runs, while `release-integrity`, `stale-prompts`, `full-battery`, `publish` and `docker` are all skipped and none is undecided. That matches the two live runs this seat dispatched by hand, 38351525685 and 38357219168: `Version PR maintenance` succeeded and the other five jobs were skipped. The reader's controls are in the same battery. The repair dispatch (`refresh_version_pr: false`) runs the audit and MAY reach `publish`. `schedule` runs `version-pr` alone, and `push` runs the audit. Two in-memory mutations must change the answer: a `release-integrity` guard that lost its negation, and a seventh job with no guard. A later edit to `release.yml` that lets this dispatch start any other job turns `check:pm-fleet-write-validate` red.
- **The ref stays `main` only, the stroke stays `alone`, and `actions: write` is minted only for it.** None of these mechanisms changed. New cases pin each one for the release stroke: one repository, `permission_actions=write`, and a release refresh beside any other op is refused.
- **The validator and executor self-tests pin both the accept and the refuse side, and the started run is read back as today.** The validator has a new battery of 22 cases. The executor's new battery has 9: one POST to `release.yml`'s dispatch endpoint carrying `{ ref: main, inputs: { refresh_version_pr: "true" } }` under the App token, landing as accepted, and every refusal sending zero requests. The dispatcher's new battery has 6: the refresh packs into ONE dispatch, its run is read back from `release.yml`'s own run list (filtered to `workflow_dispatch` on `main`), the CLI refuses an off-table stroke before anything leaves, and `--dry-run` prints the request and sends nothing.

## Design notes

- **The seat spells the inputs; the wire is built from the table.** A payload says which lane it starts, and a stroke that does not say so is refused (the card's "absent" line). The request body's `inputs` is built from `WORKFLOW_DISPATCH_INPUTS`, never from the action. So even an unjudged action naming `force` sends `refresh_version_pr: "true"` alone. A self-test case pins this.
- **On the wire every value is a string.** `"true"` is the spelling measured on the dispatch endpoint (the two runs above). A JSON boolean was not measured, so it is never sent (`dispatchInputsOnTheWire`).
- **`.github/workflows/fleet-write.yml` is unchanged.** Its mint step already reads `steps.validate.outputs.permission_actions`, the validator's stroke-scoped grant, and nothing in it names a workflow file. So this PR touches no governed surface: no workflow, no `.claude/**`, and no edit to `release.yml`.

## Tests

All of these are at `961ec7100`, the PR head.

- `pnpm check:pm-fleet-write-validate`: `✓ fleet-write/validate self-test: 152 cases pass across 11 batteries` (130 on `main`).
- `pnpm check:pm-fleet-write-execute`: `✓ fleet-write/execute self-test: 120 cases pass across 16 batteries` (111 on `main`).
- `pnpm check:pm-fleet-write-dispatch`: `✓ fleet-write/dispatch self-test: 222 cases pass across 20 batteries` (216 on `main`).
- The derived families, from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: all 37 ran, and every one exited 0. That includes `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` (`✓ dispatch-gates self-test (fast tier): 1833 cases pass`), `check:nul-bytes`, `check:self-test-wired` and `check:declaration-mirrors`. The `--ran` reconciliation answers `37 derived, 37 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN` (a derived zero, since every entry carries its exit code). The diff touches no workspace package, so there is no package build or test step.
- **Lint is narrowed, with all three pieces of evidence:**
  - eslint's own resolved config for these files (`--print-config`) carries two rules, `no-restricted-imports` and `comment-swallow/no-code-inside-block-comment`, both single-file and syntactic. Its `parserOptions` has no `project` or `projectService`, so type-aware linting is off and this diff cannot move any verdict on an untouched file.
  - `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the four changed files reports 4 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings.
  - The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Ablation, run once and not kept

Run through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on the committed `ops.mjs`. Its blob was `113cf0c32be4` at `8e3fa5f5f`; the head commit after that changes only its header comment.

- **Mutation:** the anchor `'release.yml': Object.freeze({ refresh_version_pr: true }),` became `'release.yml': Object.freeze({ refresh_version_pr: true, force: false }),`. The anchor count went from 1 to 0 and the blob from `113cf0c32be4` to `90f51ebf8297`.
- **Validator:** the self-test went red, `10 of 152 case(s) failed` (the closed table, the accepted refresh, both force cases and the token case, among others).
- **Executor:** the self-test went red, `6 of 120 case(s) failed` (the dispatch call and the force refusals).
- **Restore:** the tool reported `ok restored: blob == HEAD (113cf0c32be4) and git diff HEAD is empty`, and `git hash-object` equals `git rev-parse HEAD:scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs`.

The first ablation run found a self-test case that crashed on a refused stroke instead of failing: `tokenRepositoriesOf(null)`. Commit `8e3fa5f5f` fixed it, so the case now reds with a reason. The validator numbers above are from the re-run on that commit. The executor numbers come from the first run; the executor and `ops.mjs` were the same bytes on both runs.

## Acceptance notes

- **The ruling and AGENTS.md disagree, and this PR does not settle it.** AGENTS.md Prime Directive 15 still lists "`workflow_dispatch`-ing `release.yml` or any other publish-capable workflow" among the reserved release acts. Ruling B item 5 orders a seat to do exactly that, with `refresh_version_pr`. This PR builds the fence only (the bookkeeping lane alone, measured) and dispatches nothing. A narrowing of that sentence is a Tier H edit to `AGENTS.md`, which is outside this card's file surface. It is raised in the report for the director seat to route.
- The `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/rest-channel.md` line naming the new entry is carried by #23201 (governed `.claude/**`), not here.
- No live relay dispatch of `release.yml` was sent to try this: it would have refreshed the Version Packages PR. The evidence is the self-tests and `--dry-run` only. The first real use is the seat's operational act after the next fix lands.
